description: This case study covers New York City's protection of the Catskill and Delaware watersheds, which has let the city avoid filtering this part of its drinking water supply since 1993. The New York City Department of Environmental Protection runs the source water protection programmes and publishes their record. The US Environmental Protection Agency granted Filtration Avoidance Determinations in January and December 1993, January and May 1997, November 2002 and July 2007, and the New York State Department of Health granted the revised 2007 determination in 2014 and issued the 2017 determination on 28 December 2017. The page gathers the annual determination report, the watershed water quality annual report, the revised 2017 determination, the 2021 Long-Term Watershed Protection Program Plan and programme summary and assessment reports. Coverage is the upstate watersheds supplying New York City. Format and access: PDF reports on the DEP site and its document portal. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: the page does not give costs, and the reports are the city's own account. It is a reference case for investing in watersheds as natural infrastructure instead of a filtration plant. Related catalogue records are the Sebago watershed economic case and the Rio Camboriú watershed ROI study.
